transcript: Last night I saw Gutenberg the musical. The conceit of the show is that these two guys wrote a musical about Johann Gutenberg, who invented the printing press, and they're performing a stripped down version of it by themselves in order to attract potential producers, of course, many gags ensuably. It stars Josh Gad and Andrew Rannells, who I was lucky enough to see in book of Mormon back in 2011, which was one of the great comedic theater going experiences of my life. So I loved seeing them reunite in this piece. That allowed them to show off some of the same comedic skills and chemistry for the show itself. I had a fun time. I laughed a lot. It's very silly. Love a good framing conceit. I did get a little tired of it after a while. Maybe it was just my headspace. Maybe that they're in previews and they haven't quite found the shape of it yet. I think the intermission kind of disrupted the momentum. And it's not really necessary for the runtime. It would run like an hour and 45 minutes without it. So wonder if there's a missed opportunity in the way it was conceived, where we're going back and forth between these guys talking to the audience versus forming the show within a show. Whereas maybe I wanted more of a play that goes wrong style synergy where these two things are progressing concurrently and working in conversation with each other. We do Get some of that, but I think I wanted more for the show to reach that next level comedy status, but I still found it super clever and enjoyable. Been some discussion about whether the Tony's will consider this a new musical. There is some president for a 15 year old show being considered new. But for my money, aside from the fact that it's the same director, everything else about this feels like a pretty clear cut case of producers taking an existing piece in the canon and choosing to revive it.
